# v0.1.3 — current deployment and direct encrypted route compatibility

Fix gateway verification against the accepted W8 content-plane deployment and
add the current `other` / `near-v2` direct GLM 5.3 Flash contract in JavaScript
and Python. Provider identity is retained throughout the ticket/encrypted flow.
The reviewed release-authority gate checks boot and compose-manager quotes,
publication bindings, GPU nonce and the actual quote-bound encryption key.

The gateway still requires real DCAP, observed TLS, strict measurements,
private logs, pinned image digests and Intel `UpToDate` TCB. Provider-hop NEAR
assurance remains provider-attested; publication collateral is supplied by the
measured gateway worker, not independently fetched by the client. The direct
route does not gain a vendor-root hardware-verification claim.

Venice GLM 5.2 encrypted calls fail early while the operator withholds that
route for missing GPU evidence. Other privacy classes remain unaffected.
Examples now use an available Venice route. See `docs/release-readiness.md`
for exact checks, limitations and installation guidance.

The release workflow now accepts fresh installs of the exact JavaScript/Python
artifacts against both production gateway origins before publication. npm
publishes those same tarballs. No paid provider inference is implied by that
credential-free gateway gate.
